prompt:
The commissioning file has to carry both ends of one cable on the same sheet before the circuit is signed over, so the two photographs are taken and mounted together.

The page holds two photographs. On the left, a cable gland and terminal rail inside a switchroom cubicle, a white printed sleeve on the cable, and the room's number sign on the open door behind it. On the right, the far end of that cable landed in a machine terminal box on the shop floor, with its own sleeve. The equipment schedule lies open beneath, listing every machine by its function code, its product code and the room it stands in. Printed under the schedule is the rule the site works to: a designation is written as the function code, then a minus and the product code, then a plus and the room number, and both ends of one cable carry the designation of the machine that cable serves.

What is printed on the sleeves is not given here.
easy_question: Does this picture show a page with two photographs mounted side by side on it, one of a cable inside an electrical cubicle and one of a cable entering a machine terminal box? Answer yes or no only.

steps.ask: Read the code printed on the white cable sleeve in the left-hand photograph, then read the code printed on the white cable sleeve in the right-hand photograph. Answer with one of: the two codes read the same all the way through; the two codes share their opening section but end differently; the two codes have nothing in common.

Read the room number on the door sign behind the cubicle in the left-hand photograph, then read the part of that cubicle's cable sleeve that comes after the plus sign. Answer with one of: those two read alike; the part after the plus sign gives the number of the other room shown on this page; the part after the plus sign gives something that is not a room number on this page.
